proposals.title: Fix geocoder query so suburb listings don't collapse onto SF center
proposals.what: geocode() queries Nominatim with `{neighborhood}, {city}` which produces malformed strings like 'Fremont, CA, San Francisco' that never resolve, so listings fall back to a +/-3km jitter around SF center. Query the neighborhood/locality string as-is (drop the appended search city when the place already contains a locality), and only fall back to jitter as a last resort.
proposals.why: Fremont/Vallejo/Pleasant Hill listings showed impossible 2.6-3.0km distances from SF, wrongly passed the 20km filter, and piled onto downtown SF while a few correctly-resolved pins (El Cerrito, San Leandro) sat elsewhere — the map is internally inconsistent.

proposals.title: Cluster/spiderfy overlapping map pins
proposals.what: Add collision handling to the Leaflet map (marker clustering or spiderfy, or at minimum small offsets) so co-located price pins don't stack on top of each other unreadably.
proposals.why: Multiple price pins ($1200/$2295/$2074) render directly on top of one another near downtown SF and become illegible.

proposals.title: Add an empty state when filters exclude every listing
proposals.what: When filtered.length === 0 but listings exist, show a 'No places match — widen your price or distance' message with a reset action instead of a bare '0 of 0 fits' label over a blank void.
proposals.why: Dragging Max price to its floor left the sidebar showing 'SHORTLIST · 0 OF 0 FITS' with no message, no cards, and no map pins — a dead-end with zero guidance.

proposals.title: Surface the 409 when 'Owner replied' is clicked mid-turn
proposals.what: simulateReply ignores the fetch response; on a 409 ('A turn is already running') give the user feedback (toast/disabled-with-tooltip 'agent is mid-step, try again') instead of the button silently doing nothing.
proposals.why: Clicking 'Owner replied' during an active agent turn returned 409 and the UI gave zero feedback — only a console error; retrying after the turn settled returned 200.

proposals.title: Make the discovery Agent View feed human-readable
proposals.what: eventText falls back to raw H event type names, so the discovery feed is a wall of 'AgentEvent'/'MetricsUpdateEvent'/'RequestStartEvent'. Filter noise events and render meaningful narration (like the contact panel already does) so the live agent view actually reads as the agent thinking.
proposals.why: Discovery panel showed dozens of opaque event-type lines; the contact panel by contrast showed readable steps ('Opened WhatsApp deep link', 'Turn settled'), making the discovery feed look broken.

proposals.title: Scope discovery to the searched city, not the whole region
proposals.what: Searching 'San Francisco' starts on the regional sfbay Craigslist and returns mostly East Bay/Peninsula suburbs (Fremont, Vallejo, Concord, Martinez, San Mateo). Constrain the start URL / prompt to the searched city's neighborhoods or post-filter by distance so results match the promise.
proposals.why: Nearly all live results were 40-60km suburbs, not SF; combined with the geocode bug the 'places in San Francisco' framing is misleading.

proposals.title: Add a terminal/timeout state to the contact flow
proposals.what: After the owner reply was injected, the session ran 2+ minutes cycling raw events and never transitioned to the 'replied' success Toast; the card stayed on 'Contacting…'. Add a visible timeout/terminal state and progress so the flow can't hang silently during a demo.
proposals.why: Observed the contact card stuck on 'Contacting…' with RUNNING status past 02:11 and no success Toast within the window.

proposals.title: Lead the demo with the desktop WhatsApp negotiation on a split-screen
proposals.what: Restructure the 90s demo so the money shot is: Telegram pick -> real Mac WhatsApp desktop app (shown side-by-side) driven by the H desktop agent through a multi-turn haggle -> confirmation back in Telegram. Demote the browser search to a 5-second 'proof the session is live' flash.
proposals.why: Every Track-2 team will demo web-surfer clicking a website; an H judge finds that unremarkable. Computer-use driving a native NO-API app (WhatsApp desktop) is the un-fakeable differentiator we cannot dismiss as a browser macro. The desktop surface exists in code but isn't framed as the hero.
evidence: README.md:250 current demo script leads with map/pins

proposals.title: Prove discovery is genuinely live (or state it's pre-indexed) — never let a judge catch the cache fallback
proposals.what: Pre-warm one real live discovery session seconds before demo (or scope it to 3-4 listings that finish inside max_time_s), click the platform.hcompany.ai Agent View link on stage, and deliberately show the 'live . Craigslist (H agent)' badge. If live can't be guaranteed, be upfront that listings are pre-indexed and put all computer-use weight on the WhatsApp negotiation.
proposals.why: Their own README says Craigslist CAPTCHAs 'within minutes' and the code has a full fallbackListings() path that loads data/listings.json and rewrites permalinks. A skeptical judge's first question is 'was that map live or from a file?' — if fallback, one of two computer-use surfaces evaporates and Track-2 alignment drops.

proposals.title: Neutralize _force_send() so the agent's own send is the visible action
proposals.what: Gate the osascript 'key code 36' send behind an 'only if the agent reported replied=false' check so it never front-runs a successful agent send, and keep it silent in the demo. Show the H agent clicking the WhatsApp send button itself.
proposals.why: A fatal Q&A gotcha: 'did the H agent send the message, or your AppleScript?' If the osascript ever saves a failed agent send, the un-fakeable action wasn't done by computer-use. This single helper can reframe the strongest moment as 'they scripted it'.
evidence: contact-svc/main.py:330 _force_send called after every desktop turn

proposals.title: Retire the web UI's hardcoded 'Owner replied' string for judging
proposals.what: Judge on the Telegram path with a real teammate owner replying on real WhatsApp. Hide or disable simulateReply() (the canned 'Yes! It's available...' string) in the Next.js app during the live demo so no scripted reply is visible to the room.
proposals.why: app/page.tsx injects a hardcoded owner reply. If the flashier web UI is demoed, an H judge sees a scripted string and files the whole negotiation as fake — even though the Telegram path genuinely re-reads the real screen via a fresh H session.
evidence: app/page.tsx:291 'Owner replied' button wired to simulateReply
contact-svc/main.py:470 real reply endpoint fires a fresh screen-reading turn

proposals.title: Make the negotiation visibly haggle with real price movement
proposals.what: Script the teammate-owner to push back once (counter above ask) so the agent visibly counters under budget: e.g. asking $2450 -> agent proposes ~$2327 -> owner agrees. Surface each price step in Telegram (Owner:/Agent: lines already stream).
proposals.why: The booking is staged with a consenting teammate (correct ethics), so a judge knows the owner is a plant — the negotiation must FEEL real to survive. One message + a thumbs-up reads as scripted; visible multi-turn price movement reads as a real agent negotiating. The policy code already supports counters and a budget cap.
evidence: contact-svc/main.py:137 _negotiation_policy with discount ask + budget cap
concierge/main.py:290 streams Owner:/Agent: milestones to Telegram

proposals.title: Foreground the session-lifecycle + ops sophistication in the pitch
proposals.what: In the 90s pitch, name the hard insight out loud: 'H sessions end after they answer, so each owner reply spins up a fresh desktop session that re-reads the whole chat on screen.' Mention the 3-slot concurrency handling only if a judge probes.
proposals.why: H judges built this platform; the fresh-session-per-turn design and the max_time_s/DELETE-session/serialization work signal the team used the real API hard, not a mock. Saying it explicitly converts hidden engineering credit into visible Technicality points with the people who recognize it.
evidence: lib/discovery.ts:235 DELETE session to free concurrency slot

proposals.title: Consolidate to one front-door narrative (Telegram) to avoid a 'which is the product?' judge doubt
proposals.what: Present Telegram as THE product front door (chat in -> live agents -> chat out) and frame the Next.js app as the operator's live view you flash briefly to prove the browser session is real. Don't demo both flows as co-equal.
proposals.why: Two entry points (web app + Telegram bot) split the narrative and invite the judge to wonder which is the real thing — and the web path is the more fakeable one. A single clean story reads as a finished product, not two half-demos.
evidence: app/page.tsx full web UI with its own contact flow

proposals.title: Ship a one-command H session sweep (kill zombies before demo)
proposals.what: Add a sweep.sh (or /admin/sweep route) that GETs /api/v2/sessions?status=running and DELETEs each, then prints quota active count. Run it <2 min before demo and after any aborted rehearsal.
proposals.why: H caps at 3 concurrent sessions; a single leaked/zombie session (crash between start and delete) silently blocks discovery OR the negotiation money-shot. The plan documents a sweep but it is not coded anywhere — under stage pressure a copy-pasted curl pipe is error-prone.

proposals.title: Make explicit that the desktop negotiation needs a REAL inbound WhatsApp message
proposals.what: Rename/annotate the UI 'Owner replied' button and document that in desktop mode the agent reads the screen (main.py:203) and only replies to an actual unanswered owner message — the reply hint does not put text on screen. Put the friend on the critical path with a co-presenter backup holding the owner phone.
proposals.why: Presenters may click 'Owner replied' and wait, but the desktop turn reports awaiting_owner because no real message is on screen. This is the single most likely on-stage stall.

proposals.title: Fix README/code drift on contact surface (desktop app vs Chrome WhatsApp Web)
proposals.what: Edit README:31 to state the default is the WhatsApp desktop app (CONTACT_MODE=desktop), not Chrome WhatsApp Web via ~/.hai/chrome-profile. Keep the browser path documented only as an env-gated insurance option.
proposals.why: The stale README could send the operator to log into the wrong WhatsApp surface the morning of the demo, wasting setup time and leaving the actual desktop app unprepared.

proposals.title: Enforce single-process run mode + a /health-based go/no-go preflight
proposals.what: Document and script: run npm run dev (single Node process, the discovery store lives in globalThis), one uvicorn, one concierge; then gate the demo on curl localhost:8000/health returning desktop_ready:true, accessibility:true, screen_recording:true, whatsapp_installed:true, hai_key_present:true.
proposals.why: next start with multiple workers would not share the in-memory discovery store, dropping in-flight session ids. Revoked macOS Accessibility/Screen-Recording (reset by any python3.13 update) makes keystrokes fail silently with no error — /health is the only pre-check.

proposals.title: Harden the Telegram front-door: deleteWebhook + single consumer + kill strays
proposals.what: Before starting concierge, call deleteWebhook and pkill -f concierge/main.py so exactly one getUpdates consumer runs; add a tiny space/retry between the shortlist photo sends to avoid a Telegram 429 dropping an image.
proposals.why: Telegram getUpdates is single-consumer; a leftover process or a set webhook causes 409 conflicts and the bot appears dead. The shortlist burst (text + 3 photos + map) can trip the per-chat rate limit with no retry in send().

proposals.title: Pre-warm CDN/geocode paths and isolate the shared browse binary
proposals.what: Warm the UI once on venue wifi so Leaflet/cartocdn tiles and Nominatim geocodes cache; do not run any gstack /browse or /qa skill during the demo since make_map_image shells out to the same single browse daemon.
proposals.why: The concierge map image depends on the shared browse binary plus unpkg/cartocdn tiles and OSM geocoding — all internet + single-daemon. Contention or a blocked CDN drops the map image (non-fatal) and can grey out the UI map tiles.

proposals.title: Rehearse the network-loss and 429 fallbacks; keep a cued backup video
proposals.what: In rehearsal, kill wifi mid-discovery to confirm the cached fallback + badge flip, and force a negotiation 429 to confirm it fails visibly. Since negotiation has no cached fallback, keep a 2-4x recorded clean run cued at 0:00 on a second space, plus a paired phone hotspot.
proposals.why: Discovery degrades gracefully to cached listings, but negotiation and Telegram do not degrade — on quota/429/network loss they simply fail. The only safe net for the money-shot is the recorded video and a hotspot.

proposals.title: Embed the live H Agent View in-app, beside the streaming timeline
proposals.what: AgentViewPanel receives agentViewUrl but only renders a text link. Add an <iframe src={agentViewUrl}> pane next to the cyan step timeline so judges watch the real browser being driven live inside your own UI. Keep the existing 'Watch live' link as a guaranteed fallback and hide the iframe on load-error/timeout in case platform.hcompany.ai sends X-Frame-Options.
proposals.why: Turns the strongest browser-surface moment from an invisible link into something the room actually sees; safe fallback means it can never break the demo.

proposals.title: Desktop Cam: frame the real WhatsApp window during negotiation
proposals.what: The desktop agent already activates WhatsApp and force-sends via osascript. Add a /demo presenter layout (or OBS scene) that mirrors the actual WhatsApp desktop window on the projector while the agent types + sends, plus a slim in-app overlay ('H desktop agent is operating WhatsApp'). Mostly staging, no change to the H session code.
proposals.why: The un-fakeable money shot: judges watch a cursor type and hit send in a real Mac app. This is the single biggest 'whoa' and it's currently happening off-frame.

proposals.title: 'Saved you $X' negotiation-win callout on booking
proposals.what: Listing price and the agent's agreed_price / viewing_time already flow back through _apply_turn_result and the concierge 'Booked!' message. On booking, show a big 'Negotiated $2450 -> $2300 · saved $150/mo · viewing Sat 2pm' callout in-app and in the Telegram confirmation.
proposals.why: Proves the agent didn't just message an owner, it haggled and won real money — the line judges repeat back.

proposals.title: Full-screen 'THE AGENT IS NEGOTIATING FOR YOU' state with real chat bubbles
proposals.what: Owner/agent turns already arrive tagged (classify() handles owner:/agent:; contact-svc emits Owner:/Agent: events). Promote the small contacting side-panel to a projector-readable hero overlay that renders the turns as green/gray WhatsApp-style bubbles in a phone frame, with a big 'Negotiating…' headline and the live timer.
proposals.why: Makes 'it's really having a back-and-forth conversation' legible from the back of the room, at the demo's emotional peak.

proposals.title: Sound + confetti cues on send and on 'Booked!'
proposals.what: There's no audio today and the reply Toast is silent. Add a Web Audio 'send' blip when the agent fires a message and a triumphant chime + confetti burst when phase becomes replied/booked. No assets required (Web Audio API + CSS/canvas confetti).
proposals.why: Sound at the climax is literally what makes a room react audibly; costs almost nothing.

proposals.title: Persistent '2 computer-use agents' HUD badge
proposals.what: Add a header chip with a browser glyph and a desktop glyph that pulse when each surface is live (browser during discovering, desktop during contacting). Reuse the existing .pulse keyframe.
proposals.why: Continuously advertises the rare dual computer-use claim instead of relying on the narrator to say it once.

proposals.title: Staggered live pin-drop animation as listings arrive
proposals.what: finishDiscovery currently sets all listings at once so the map pops fully formed. Drop the pins one-by-one with a short bounce while the Agent View streams steps, so the map visibly fills live as the agent scrolls Craigslist. Purely front-end/cosmetic, no risk to the H session.
proposals.why: Turns a static reveal into a suspenseful 'it's finding them right now' beat.

proposals.title: Telegram 'typing…' beats + live-streamed negotiation, optional QR to H live view
proposals.what: The concierge already forwards Owner:/Agent: lines to chat. Add sendChatAction:typing before each agent line and pace them so the judge's own phone lights up with the back-and-forth in real time. Optionally attach the H live-view link as a QR so judges can open the session on their own phones.
proposals.why: Makes the 'I just texted it and it did the errand' hook tangible in the judge's hand during the pitch.

proposals.title: Kill the "AgentEvent" wall — humanize the Agent View stream
proposals.what: In lib/discovery.ts `eventText()` (and the twin `_event_text` in contact-svc/main.py), most H events carry no message/text/thought field, so the function falls through to `return String(type)` and the marquee panel renders 20+ identical lines: "AgentEvent", "AgentEvent", "MetricsUpdateEvent". Replace with (1) a lookup map that turns known types into human milestones (AgentStartedEvent -> "Agent online — browser booted", RequestStartEvent -> "Dispatching to H web-surfer", etc.), and (2) drop events that resolve to a bare type name so only meaningful steps show. Prefer surfacing the agent's actual thought/action when present.
proposals.why: The Agent View is the whole 'wow' of the demo — it is meant to read like a machine working. Right now it reads like a raw debug log of repeated class names, which actively cheapens the marquee feature. See evidence: after 48s the panel is a solid column of 'AgentEvent'/'MetricsUpdateEvent'.

proposals.title: De-dupe + throttle the event feed so steps land like beats
proposals.what: Even after humanizing, collapse consecutive identical/near-identical events into one line with a count ("Scanning listings x6"), and skip pure MetricsUpdateEvent telemetry. In AgentViewPanel.tsx optionally reveal each new event with a short fade/slide so lines arrive as discrete beats rather than a jumping list.
proposals.why: The stream currently emits many low-signal events per second; a wall that scrolls faster than a judge can read feels like noise, not progress. A handful of clean, sequential milestones reads as 'the agent is deliberately doing steps.'

proposals.title: Make the map alive during discovery — scanning sweep + ghost pins
proposals.what: During the 'discovering' phase the entire right ~75% of the screen is a dead, empty map for 60-120s — the exact window a judge is watching most. Add motion: a subtle radial/scan-line sweep over the map center, and drop 3-6 faint pulsing 'ghost' price pins that resolve into real pins when results land. Tie it to phase==='discovering' in app/page.tsx.
proposals.why: The Agent View panel says the machine is working, but the biggest surface on screen contradicts it by sitting perfectly still and empty. Filling that void with restrained motion makes the whole app feel like it is actively searching the city.

proposals.title: Stronger idle/hero state instead of a dead map + tiny dashed box
proposals.what: On first load the map is empty and the sidebar shows only a small dashed box reading 'Enter your search and the agent will scout Craigslist live.' Add a centered hero overlay on the map: product name + tagline + a compact 3-step 'how it works' (Scout Craigslist -> Shortlist on map -> Negotiate on WhatsApp), or pre-seed the map with the cached listing pins so the canvas is never empty. Fades out once a search starts.
proposals.why: The idle screen is the first frame a judge sees; right now it communicates almost nothing about what the product does and looks unfinished (huge blank map). A hero frame sets the stakes and makes the reveal land harder.

proposals.title: Add a one-line product tagline under the brand lockup
proposals.what: The header is just 'Homeless' + 'APARTMENTAGENT' with no explanation. Add a single muted mono/sans tagline beneath it, e.g. 'An AI agent that scouts Craigslist and negotiates your lease over WhatsApp.' One line, ~11-12px, --muted.
proposals.why: 'Homeless' is a memorable but opaque name; without a tagline a judge has to infer the value prop from the UI. One sentence removes all ambiguity and reads premium/intentional.

proposals.title: Fix the muddy-brown loading button
proposals.what: The primary button while searching is amber at opacity .55 (disabled), which renders as a muddy brown behind 'Agent is searching Craigslist…'. Give the working state its own treatment: keep the amber bright and add an animated progress shimmer / indeterminate bar, or a subtle pulsing border — rather than dimming it.
proposals.why: The button is the visual anchor of the sidebar during the whole live-search moment; a dull brown reads as broken/disabled, undercutting the 'agent is actively working' story the panel is telling.

proposals.title: Recolor the Agent View 'RUNNING' badge to cyan for role consistency
proposals.what: The panel establishes a strict 3-role color system (amber = brand/action, cyan = live agent telemetry, green = contact). But the Agent View footer 'RUNNING' badge is rendered amber (`.badge.live`), clashing with the cyan telemetry theme of that very panel. Give the in-panel status badge a cyan variant.
proposals.why: Within one cyan-framed telemetry panel, an amber status pill breaks the self-imposed color grammar and makes the palette look accidental rather than systematic. Judges reading design intent notice the inconsistency.

proposals.title: Format Telegram messages with bold prices/titles (Markdown)
proposals.what: concierge/main.py sends everything as plain text (no parse_mode anywhere). The shortlist lines '1) title — $2450/mo 2BR · Neighborhood' and photo captions are flat. Add parse_mode Markdown/HTML and bold the price and title, and structure the shortlist as clean rows (e.g. *$2450/mo* — 2BR · Mission Dolores). Bold the '✅ Booked!' and agreed price too.
proposals.why: The Telegram thread is a second demo surface (screenshared alongside the web UI). Bold prices and tidy structure make the chat read like a polished product notification instead of a debug echo, at near-zero effort.

proposals.title: Match the Telegram map pins to the web app's amber best-match pin
proposals.what: The Telegram map image (make_map_image) uses hollow cyan ring pins for every listing. The web app distinguishes the best-match with a glowing filled amber pin. Render the perfect/best-match pin in the Telegram map as a filled amber pin too, so the two surfaces share one visual language.
proposals.why: Consistency across surfaces reads as a designed system. Right now the Telegram map and the web map use different pin styles/colors, so they look like two separate hacks rather than one product.
